stem:
Lachlan, 7 (24 kg), has been in a generalised tonic-clonic seizure for 25 minutes. He has already had two benzodiazepine doses: buccal midazolam from paramedics, then IV midazolam in hospital. His airway is held with a jaw thrust, SpO2 is 96% on oxygen and glucose is 6.1 mmol/L.

What is needed now?

options.label: A
options.explanation: RCH allows at most two benzodiazepine doses, counting pre-hospital doses. The buccal and IV doses already make two, and a third adds respiratory depression.

options.label: B
options.explanation: RCH reserves pyridoxine for infants up to 6 months old whose seizures are refractory to standard anticonvulsants. Lachlan is 7.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Rapid sequence intubation with an anaesthetic infusion is the step for seizures refractory to second-line treatment. His airway is currently maintained.

options.label: D
options.text: CT brain before any more drugs
options.explanation: Imaging does not stop the seizure. Treat it first; imaging can be considered once he is stable.

options.label: E
options.explanation: Correct. After two benzodiazepine doses, give a second-line agent such as levetiracetam 40-60 mg/kg IV (max 4.5 g) over 5 minutes (phenytoin is an alternative) and call senior airway help.

context: Status epilepticus: at most two benzodiazepine doses, pre-hospital ones included, then a second-line drug (levetiracetam or phenytoin) while senior airway help is called.
